newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-TWO TURKISH CLUBS IN NEXT CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TWO TURKISH CLUBS IN NEXT CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE.

text.p: Two Turkish clubs will be eligible to compete in the expanded European Champions' League next season, UEFA said on Friday.
The announcement means that Greece will have only one team in the competition.

A problem arose because Turkey and Greece were level in eighth place on the co-efficient points system used by UEFA to evaluate the rankings of each country which in turn determines how many teams from each are eligible to take part in the competition.
The top eight countries in the rankings can each field two teams in the competition -- one seeded and one entering the qualifying rounds.
Countries ranked ninth to 16th can field one team in the Champions' League which will comprise 24 teams for the first time.

The ranking system is based on points gained in European club competitions over the past five years and UEFA used a tie-break method of taking this season's co-efficient points into consideration and on that basis Turkey had 7.75 points and Greece 3.75.

UEFA also confirmed that if Juventus, Ajax, Manchester United or Borussia Dortmund won the European Cup this season and finished third in their respective leagues, then Italy, the Netherlands, Germany or England would have three teams in the competition next season.
Meanwhile, UEFA said they are to continue with their most junior competition, the InterToto Cup, for at least another season.
The competition, which is used as a qualifying tournament for the UEFA Cup, has caused problems for some of the major European countries whose clubs are not interested in it.

UEFA president Lennart Johansson conceeded that point on Friday but added: "The executive committee are keen to continue with the experiment of the Cup in its present format and then analyse the situation and decide on its future at a later date. It has caused problems for the bigger countries but clubs from the smaller countries have welcomed it."
Johansson also announced the introduction of an indoor European soccer championship for national teams in 1998 following two world championships for indoor soccer or "FUTSAL" in recent years.
